LANDING PR for #434's DESIGN (documents only): a PROPOSED addendum to decision 0006 (ending an attempt's process proves nothing about its effects, and a retry needs evidence) and research entry 0021 (the effect classes and transport paths, and what each reports on a deadline kill, a lost result, a pre-session refusal, a partial side effect and a cleanup failure). The addendum is for the operator to accept; nothing is built. #434 stays open for the build.

The branch story-434-design ends at 4605f212, over three commits off main 3ad0f66c. Main is now 07a620ee, and the merge is clean.
- 6a75178e: the design story's draft. Its review returned a SECURITY-HOLD.
- e9abde02: fix round 434e.
  - A lost result parks; "no result was read" covers the driver's synthesized no-result failure, stdout failing after start, unreadable JSON and a wrong proto.
  - A transport-limit end (decision 0079) never retries.
  - A replay declaration stands only on a whole, site-scoped identity.
  - The authority for retry is named.
  The review returned residual at medium.
- 4605f212: the second fix round. An invocation error after the spawn is a lost result, and a lost handshake still parks. The review ruled residual at low.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks below. It reports each finding. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns.

Judge:
1. That the retry matrix never retries without evidence of the executor's own receipt, and parks otherwise. Its cells: pre-session refusal, process timeout, lost result, partial side effect, cleanup failure.
2. That accepted decision 0079 stands over the proposed addendum (a transport-limit end never retries), and that nothing weakens #403's settlement.
3. That every claim about today's behaviour in research 0021 points at code that says so, at the base.
4. That each ruling carries an enforcement binding naming the tests the build must add, including the issue's acceptance cases. One is a fake executor that commits a marker and loses its result, with and without a deadline kill: it is reconciled or parks, and never commits twice. Another is a deduplicating executor that acts once across retries.
5. That the open questions are under Asked, and that the documents say what they do not claim: no general exactly-once, and no local cleanup taken as proof of remote rollback.
6. That the second fix round's carried LOWs and INFOs are listed for the PR.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051, so the contribution gate can vouch for it.

For the implement phase only: if a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding in the documents. Documents only: no Rust, script, test or workflow. Then run, all clean: typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it -- doc_truth:: decisions_index:: research_registry:: status_pages:: house_prose::; git diff --check.

Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Run every command in the foreground: never background a command or schedule a wakeup, because a headless seat ends when it waits.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including both supported operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
```

members.adversarial:
Read-only adversarial review of all four document changes at 4605f212 against 3ad0f66c, including both fix rounds, with the main movement through 07a620ee inspected. Read README and decisions 0004, 0005, 0006, 0051, 0053, 0071 and 0079; checked the load-bearing process, adapter, engine, sequence, fold, identity and bundle citations at the stated base. Frozen contracts, fixtures, policy and reference have no changes. No tracked file changed and no commit made. No unresolved high/critical finding found. The earlier hold is answered: transport-limit ends always park under accepted 0079 ruling 3; missing executor results include no-result-file, signal and post-spawn invocation errors; composite deduplication declarations refuse compilation; replay authority is pinned operator data and the driver echo is delivery evidence only. Cleanup settlement is required before replay and is never remote rollback. All seven proposed rulings carry build bindings; marker-loss with and without a kill, post-spawn prompt failure, deduplicated retries, fallback, cleanup refusal and compatibility have specified tests. These are future bindings, not executed behavior tests. Status remains proposed, the authority and other open choices are under Asked, and general exactly-once is disclaimed.

Confirmed carried findings for the PR (also already listed in the design-story ledger):
L1 LOW, 0071 rulings 2 and 9, research 0021:77-78 and :200; 0006:255-258 and :268. Input: a settled dialect_exec verify step returns exit 1, or exits 0 without a result file. The inventory predicts protocol Failed and attempt retry. At adapters.rs:6851-6882 it instead sends Succeeded with result fail/pass before the generic error/file arms; sequence.rs:482-483 and :512-519 process the declared result, with no attempt retry from that exit. A signal also reaches this synthesis as exit -1. Inventory the dialect path separately and state explicitly how the proposed lost-result rule covers a signal there.
L2 LOW, ruling 9, research 0021:73; 0006:254 and :266. Input: a driver hangs before capabilities, max_attempts=2, watchdog kills it, cleanup settles. Those sentences predict that a Lost handshake parks today. process.rs:460-466 checks timed_out first and reports Failed, so engine.rs:900-935 retries. Qualify the historical claim with deadline precedence; the proposed timeout row already parks it.
L3 LOW, ruling 5, 0006:236-245 versus :266. Input: a missing-secret refusal sends Accepted then Failed before spawning (adapters.rs:6554-6572). There is no executor receipt and none of ruling 1's three pre-execution disjuncts holds; its rule therefore disallows retry, while the matrix permits it. Add the driver-known pre-invocation refusal as a separate disjunct, retaining failed_to_start solely for chain descent. This contradiction is toward refusal, not a fail-open exception.
L4 LOW, rulings 2 and 9, 0006:249-250 and :268; research 0021's ends table. Input: a driver commits a marker and sends status succeeded with result absent/null, max_attempts=2, settled cleanup. process.rs:665-669 synthesizes Failed and today retries; the inventory omits this arm and the binding covers no result read, whereas this is Ended::Reached at :655. Explicitly classify the incomplete receipt and name its binding. The general whole/readable receipt requirement is stricter, so this is an enumeration/binding gap rather than an authorized fail-open retry.
I1 INFO, carried ruling 5 summary drift, decisions README:84. Input: declared/delivered lost result with unresolved cleanup, or engine restart. The summary's replay exception appears to permit retry, whereas 0006 ruling 5 and :367-368 always park. Carry those exclusions in the summary.
I2 INFO, carried citation mismatch, research 0021:104-105. Looking up the quoted answers neither yes nor no in 0053 ruling 5 does not find it; the exact quotation is at 0053:94 in the rejected-alternative paragraph. Correct its attribution.

Additional finding L5 LOW, ruling 5, research 0021:41 versus 0006:352-362 and :487-494. Input: a declared single deduplicating exec, delivered identity echoed by its driver, settled deadline kill, and no command-level acknowledgement. Ruling 4 authorizes retry, while research finding 6 describes executor acknowledgement as required. Align the planned finding with the chosen declaration/driver-delivery rule and identify the command receipt as the Asked alternative. The addendum explains its reason: no channel today carries the command's own word before it acts; that reason is carried, not treated as actual executor acknowledgement.

Foreground checks observed in this seat: typos --hidden passed; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones passed; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it -- doc_truth:: decisions_index:: research_registry:: status_pages:: house_prose:: passed (44 tests, zero failures); git diff --check and git diff 3ad0f66c..HEAD --check passed; tracked worktree stayed clean. No fault executor was run. Verdict residual, maximum low, no security residual. #434 remains the build issue; no implementation or acceptance of the proposed addendum is claimed.

Read README, decisions 0004/0005/0051/0071/0079, the complete proposed addendum and research entry, prior panel/chief records, and the load-bearing cited production paths at the stated base. No tracked changes or commits. git diff --check passed; production code, frozen contracts, fixtures, policy and reference are unchanged. No build or tests were run by this read-only seat; the prior review records report 44 prose tests and document gates passing. All seven addendum rulings carry enforcement bindings; the marker-loss cases (deadline, no file, post-spawn prompt-write error), deduplicating executor, transport-limit exclusion and unresolved cleanup each have proposed tests. These are build obligations, not evidence of an implementation. Accepted 0079 retains unconditional transport-limit parking and #403 settlement still precedes every retry. Status remains proposed; Asked records unresolved choices; no general exactly-once or local-cleanup-as-rollback claim is made. The deliberately named authority choice is the operator's pinned declaration plus command placeholder and driver echo, not the command's own acknowledgement; the stricter executor receipt is explicitly under Asked (0006:487-494). That distinction must remain visible in the PR.
Carried second-round findings for the PR, independently confirmed, with no additional finding above low:
L1 LOW, 0071 rulings 2 and 9: research 0021:77-78 and :200 apply ordinary exec outcomes to dialect_exec. adapters.rs:6851-6882 instead returns protocol Succeeded with a synthesized success/failure word before the nonzero-exit and missing-file arms. Nonzero exit, signal (-1), and exit 0 with no result file follow that dialect path; sequence.rs:482-483 and :512-519 then decide using the result vocabulary, rather than automatically retrying from protocol Failed. Inventory this distinct path and qualify the generic rows. The addendum's signal/no-result classification and run_seat_with binding (0006:255-259, :268) also need to state how this earlier dialect return is treated.
L2 LOW, ruling 9: research 0021:73 and 0006:254/:266 say a lost handshake parks today without the deadline qualification. eof_outcome at process.rs:460-466 checks timed_out first: a driver hanging before capabilities reaches Lost but reports Failed(deadline) and can retry today once cleanup settles. Transport refusal also takes precedence in finish. Qualify today's claim; the proposed timeout law already parks this case.
L3 LOW, ruling 5: 0006:236-245's refusal definition excludes a driver refusal after accepted but before invocation, while the pre-session matrix at :266 permits retry. Missing-secret, charter and pre-spawn invocation refusals send accepted (adapters.rs:6553-6597, :6675-6702). Add the missing pre-invocation disjunct; keep failed_to_start as the model-chain predicate. The narrower definition is conservative, so this inconsistency does not weaken a refusal.
L4 LOW, ruling 9: reached at process.rs:665-669 makes a succeeded result without payload Failed, eligible for retry today. It is not a whole receipt under 0006:230-235, yet the lost-result inventory omits it and the proposed no-result-read binding does not cover Ended::Reached. Explicitly classify it and inventory it in research 0021.
I1 INFO: docs/decisions/README.md:84's retry-exception summary omits engine-restart and unresolved-cleanup exclusions present in rulings 4/5. Carry these qualifications into the summary.
I2 INFO: research 0021:104-105 attributes 'answers neither yes nor no' to decision 0053 ruling 5; the quotation is in the rejected-alternative paragraph at 0053:94. Correct the attribution.
These are the prior chief's four LOWs and two INFOs, preserved at their honest severities for the landing PR. No security residual identified by this correctness seat.
members.glm:
Read-only correctness review of the #434 landing design (docs only). git diff 3ad0f66c..4605f212 is exactly four files (proposed 0006 addendum, research 0021, decisions index row, research index row); no Rust, script, test or workflow; contracts/, reference/, fixtures/ and policy/ untouched; merge-tree into 07a620ee is conflict-free (one changed-in-both file, docs/decisions/README.md, different rows). No tracked file changed and no commit made.

JUDGED. (1) Matrix: the six rows of 0006:262-275 retry only on receipt (partial side effect) or refusal before execution (pre-session), and park on every uncertain end - timeout and lost result retry only under ruling 4's conditions (settled cleanup, byte-exact echoed identity equal to effect/requested.idempotency_key, kill-or-lost end, never an engine restart or transport-limit end), while transport limit, cleanup failure and engine restart park always; 'Termination alone never makes one' (0006:244-245).
